text:
sara-support: Heads up — new customer Acera reporting their API token isn't in the prod project console (acera-prod-9). They can call the API with the token we issued but the key isn't visible in the customer's prod project dashboard. Looks like it landed in a sandbox project instead. Anyone seen routing like this?

miguel-oncall: can you drop the tenant and provision job id? I can check the provisioning logs.

sara-support: tenant: acera.ai, provision job id: 2026-03-12-874. Customer said the console shows keys under `redwood-sbx-1122` but their target is `acera-prod-9`.

priya-enginfra: pulling logs for job 2026-03-12-874 now. quick note: provisioning creates a tenant claim that must match `org_id` in the claim mapping. if that's wrong, keys get attached to default sandbox.

deploy-bot: Provisioner job 2026-03-12-874 status: FAILED -> retry attempted, FINAL_STATUS: COMPLETED_WITH_WARNINGS. Error snippet: `claim_mismatch: expected org=acera-prod-9 got org=redwood-sbx-1122`

priya-enginfra: aha — the claim shows org=redwood-sbx-1122. looks like an env var permutation during the provisioning run. grabbing the full trace...

priya-enginfra: ```
2026-03-12T15:02:11Z Provisioner[874] INFO starting job for tenant=acera.ai target=acera-prod-9
2026-03-12T15:02:13Z Provisioner[874] WARN env.PROJECT_OVERRIDE=redwood-sbx-1122
2026-03-12T15:02:15Z Provisioner[874] ERROR claim_mismatch: generated_claim.org=redwood-sbx-1122 expected=acera-prod-9
```

emma-cs: I told Acera we'd investigate and give a timeline. Can we give them a temporary token for prod while this is fixed? They have an enterprise POC tomorrow.

miguel-oncall: yes we can issue a short-lived token. but prefer rotating the misattached key so there's no orphaned credential. steps:
1) revoke the key attached to redwood-sbx-1122
2) re-run the provisioner with sanitized env (remove PROJECT_OVERRIDE) or explicitly set `PROJECT_ID=acera-prod-9`
3) attach newly created key to acera-prod-9 and confirm appears in console
4) issue temporary prod token with `--ttl 4h` for the customer if they need immediate access

priya-enginfra: I'm going to re-run the job with the correct env now. before I do, can someone confirm we have no automated rollback that would delete the sandbox key? I want to avoid killing a key they might still be using.

miguel-oncall: we don't auto-delete keys on re-provision, so step 1 should be explicit revoke. I'll revoke the sandbox one once new key is active.

priya-enginfra: re-run started: `provisioner start --job 2026-03-12-874 --PROJECT_ID=acera-prod-9 --force-claim`

deploy-bot: Provisioner job 2026-03-12-874.2 queued

priya-enginfra: new key created: `rk_live_3b6f...` (created and attached to acera-prod-9). console link: https://console.redwood.ai/projects/acera-prod-9/keys (internal)

emma-cs: sent temp token to the customer with 4h TTL and told them we'll rotate to a permanent one shortly. :thumbsup:

miguel-oncall: revoking old key from redwood-sbx-1122 now.

miguel-oncall: done — old key revoked. Confirmed: calls with the old sandbox token fail with 401. new prod token works and is visible in the customer's console.

sara-support: thanks all. Can we add a small guard in provisioner to prevent `PROJECT_OVERRIDE` leaking into claims? file a quick follow-up ticket?

priya-enginfra: filing ticket now — infra #INT-4621: prevent PROJECT_OVERRIDE from being used in claim generation. includes repro (job 2026-03-12-874) and patch suggestion.

emma-cs: Acera is happy and POC is back on track. they asked if we can document the temporary token flow for CS in case we need to do this again. I'll make a short runbook.

miguel-oncall: nice. small follow-ups: add alert when claim_mismatch occurs and include original env dump in debug logs (scrub secrets).

sara-support: agreed. closing thread when ticket INT-4621 is created. thanks everyone.
